evals.prompt: Run RoB 2 on this randomised trial before I cite it — I want the risk of bias per domain and an overall judgement, with the evidence for each answer.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Names the specific result assessed and states that the effect of interest is assignment to intervention (ITT); Answers the signalling questions Y/PY/PN/N/NI with page or section citations; Derives each of the five domain judgements from the RoB 2 algorithm, not from an impression; Applies the overall rule: any High domain makes the overall judgement High.
expectations: Names the specific result assessed and states that the effect of interest is assignment to intervention (ITT)
Answers the signalling questions Y/PY/PN/N/NI with page or section citations
Derives each of the five domain judgements from the RoB 2 algorithm, not from an impression
Applies the overall rule: any High domain makes the overall judgement High

evals.prompt: This randomised trial reports a big effect, but 22% of the treatment arm dropped out versus 4% of controls and the headline outcome is not the one in the registry. Assess the risk of bias in the trial and tell me how much that undermines the result.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Maps differential attrition to the missing-outcome-data domain and outcome switching to selection of the reported result; Judges the affected domains High and therefore the overall judgement High; States what the study can still support (hypothesis-generating) and what it cannot.
expectations: Maps differential attrition to the missing-outcome-data domain and outcome switching to selection of the reported result
Judges the affected domains High and therefore the overall judgement High
States what the study can still support (hypothesis-generating) and what it cannot

evals.prompt: Is this randomised controlled trial trustworthy enough to base a recommendation on? Assess its methodological weaknesses domain by domain and tell me what a replication would need to do differently.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Applies the five Cochrane RoB 2 domains rather than an ad-hoc quality checklist; Produces per-domain judgements of Low risk / Some concerns / High risk with supporting evidence; Ends with a follow-up section naming what a stronger replication must change.
expectations: Applies the five Cochrane RoB 2 domains rather than an ad-hoc quality checklist
Produces per-domain judgements of Low risk / Some concerns / High risk with supporting evidence
Ends with a follow-up section naming what a stronger replication must change

evals.prompt: Across the whole literature, how certain are we that this intervention works? GRADE the body of evidence for each outcome and give me a summary of findings.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Rates certainty across the whole body of evidence per outcome with GRADE domains; Does not produce a single-study risk-of-bias table (evidence-appraisal behaviour).
expectations: Rates certainty across the whole body of evidence per outcome with GRADE domains
Does not produce a single-study risk-of-bias table (evidence-appraisal behaviour)

evals.prompt: A vendor claims their model scores 91.2% on GSM8K and beats GPT-4o. Audit that claim for contamination, baseline pinning, seed variance and cherry-picked metrics.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Audits the benchmark-specific integrity domains and emits a reliability score with risk tags; Does not apply Cochrane RoB 2 domains to a leaderboard claim (benchmark-model-claims behaviour).

Does not apply Cochrane RoB 2 domains to a leaderboard claim (benchmark-model-claims behaviour)
